uti vellet. Sic populorum nomine veniebant in V. T.

fidem ingressi, Deo Israëlis se gubernandos tradide-
rant. 2.) Quando reliquiæ populorum designantur hoc
loco, præsupponit Spiritus Sanctus, ex persecutionibus
præcedentibus maximam eorum partem fuisse excisam &
absumptam; quorum pauci superstites reliquias eorum
faciebant. Joel. 2: 32. Proin etiam hic articulus in
theologiâ prophetica venit observandus; Deum quandoquidem
spoliatores ecclesiæ tradere credentibus spoliandos.
Ezech. 39: 10. atque tale quid etiam exspectandum
populis, regnum Christi constituentibus post judicium
Judæorum, quando judicaret Deus monarchiam
illam gentilium, gravissimarum persecutionum ante au-
torem. Conf. Psal. 68: 13. Jes. 53: 12.
§. 3. Verum ne hanc despoliationem gentium putemus
solam judicii, à principe adversario sumendi, cau-
sam, addit etiam alias rationes; iram illam Dei, talionem
præcipientis, irritantes: quarum prior est Sanguis
hominis vindicandus. Vox אדם[?] hic accipitur à multis
collectivè, singulare pro plurali, ut illi vitio vertatur
quod omnia cæde impleverit. Verum hoc crimen sub
violentiâ terræ, urbi, omnibusque eam incolentibus
illatâ comprehenditur. Ego p[illegible, ~3 letters]s hic singularem aliquem
hominem intelligi puto, [illegible, ~3 letters] cuius nece reatum
sanguinis contraxit, in principe, pœnitentiam facti ne-
gante, non sine supplicio prætereundum. Neque sine
mysterio hanc vocem adhibuisse Deum putandum est;

page.notes: Ink blot covers part of line 3 of the last paragraph ("Ego p…s hic") and the word before "cuius"; those readings are marked illegible. The Hebrew word after "Vox" (rendered as אדם[?]) is hard to read in the scan and should be checked against the original. The catchword at the lower right is read as "lâ" and is uncertain. Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout (e.g. "Jes."). Running head reads "HABAKUK"; the chapter marker "CAP. II: 5-8." at the top right is not included as it is not part of the running title.
